claims.statement: Polish law places approval and building-electrical documentation with the condominium, cooperative or property manager and provides for a qualified electrical expert report; the founder can seek an association-approved concession to build and operate the shared charging riser and capacity allocator, although the concession cannot unlawfully block residents' statutory application rights.

When expert analysis finds a charger requires a changed connection agreement or rebuilt electrical installation, Polish law makes the applicant cover those costs; meanwhile the recast buildings directive requires substantial pre-cabling in new or deeply renovated residential parking, so duplicated one-off applications and unmanaged capacity are a current, measurable capital and delay problem.

The immediate payer is the resident requesting a charger, because statute can assign necessary upgrade costs to that applicant; the association or developer is the budget owner for common riser and pre-cabling at renovation, triggered by several requests or new-building obligations.

contrary_evidence: For sub-11 kW requests Polish rules may treat approval as ordinary management, so residents may install independently instead of joining one concession.
Newer buildings may already be pre-cabled, reducing the infrastructure-control wedge to software billing and load balancing.

economics.acquisition_route: Through electrical installers and property managers, fund one building-wide expert study and resident demand survey, then propose an association vote granting a 7-10 year non-exclusive operating agreement for the shared riser, load controller and billing layer.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Pilot three buildings, grow through property managers to 400 buildings averaging 40 active ports at PLN 35 monthly net service revenue for PLN 6.72m recurring revenue, plus installation margin; if hardware is resident- or lender-funded, retained equity and cash could plausibly exceed PLN 5m in 6-8 years.
economics.founder_time: Founder spends 2-3 hours daily on demand scoring, load allocation and property-manager channels; the parents' or partner electricians perform design, inspection and installation.
economics.gross_margin_basis: Recurring billing and load-management software can exceed 70% gross margin, while installation is lower; blended preliminary target is 40-55% without carrying building hardware on the balance sheet.
economics.payback: Use resident deposits or building finance for equipment; target resident all-in cost below a bespoke one-off installation and building-level infrastructure payback within 24-36 months from setup and monthly fees.
economics.pricing: PLN 2,000-5,000 connection fee per parking space, hardware at cost plus 15-25%, and PLN 30-60 per month per active charger for metering, billing and capacity allocation.
economics.retention_or_repeat: The operating agreement and shared electrical infrastructure persist for years; each new EV-owning resident joins the same managed capacity pool.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Building-level operating agreements secure local distribution, and charging/load histories improve safe capacity allocation and upgrade timing across a property-manager portfolio.
fingerprint.customer: Polish condominium associations, housing cooperatives and multifamily property managers receiving multiple resident EV-charger requests.
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Property-manager portfolios and electrical installers bring the first request; an association-wide expert study converts a one-off inquiry into a building system.
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Shared electrical riser, dynamic load allocation and resident billing under a multi-year building operating agreement, funded by setup and monthly port fees.
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: Residents pay when connecting a parking space and monthly while charging; the association pays only for optional common upgrades or study work.
fingerprint.problem_trigger: The second or third charger request, a major renovation, or an expert finding that one-off connections require common electrical upgrades.

founder_fit: The parents' installation company provides field capability and local property-manager credibility.
Load allocation, billing analytics and portfolio rollout use the founder's data and automation strengths.
Resident deposits and contracted electricians can keep capital within the founder's means and the founder out of daily installation work.
risks: Association voting and procurement can be slow, political and relationship-intensive.
An exclusive or discriminatory agreement could conflict with resident charging rights or competition law.
Fire-safety, metering, energy resale and connection rules may require approvals or licensed partners.

structure.control_point: Association-approved operating rights over the shared charging riser, load allocator and resident billing layer
structure.critical_dependency: A lawful building agreement and sufficient electrical headroom or financeable upgrade

thesis: Convert fragmented resident charger requests into one building-wide capacity system: trade an expert study and financed riser plan for multi-year operating rights, then allocate scarce connection capacity and bill each joining parking space.
title: Condo Charging Micro-Concessions
uncertainties: Counsel must test whether the proposed operating term and pricing preserve all statutory resident rights.
Resident density, willingness to prepay and property-manager sales-cycle length are unknown.
The boundary between private charging service, electricity resale and regulated metering needs verification.
